$comment: Impressum (§5 DDG, formerly §5 TMG) and the details the privacy policy
needs.
!!! Nobody can invent these details for you. While null stands here,
/impressum/ and /datenschutz/ show a visible notice in that spot
instead of a value, and `make check` reports it as an ERROR — a page
with a made-up address would be worse than one that says the detail is
still missing.
Legal form: a group without a legal form is an unregistered
association or a group of private individuals. In that case you name
an authorised representative with their address. A PO box or c/o
address is not enough — it has to be an address where legal documents
can be served.
Not legal advice: the text on both pages is a basis for a site without
a form, without analytics and without cookies. Have it looked over
before the domain goes live.
responsible: name of the authorised representative, e.g. "Robin Starkgraff".
entity: only fill this in if there is a legal form (e. V., GbR, UG) —
otherwise leave it null, and only the person is shown.
street/postalCode/city: an address where legal documents can be served.
phone: optional, but a second route besides email is welcome.
vatId: only if there is one (VAT ID under §27a UStG).
publishAddressInSchema: should the full address additionally travel
into the structured data (JSON-LD)? The default is false. It is in the
Impressum because the law demands it; in the JSON-LD Google would read
it as the group's address and could show it in maps and the knowledge
panel — and it is a private address, not a venue. Set it to true if
that is what you want.
publishPhoneInSchema: the same for the phone number, and for the same
reason. It used to sit in the JSON-LD without anyone being asked while
the address was protected — that was a contradiction, not a decision.
The default is now false: the number is in the Impressum and on
/kontakt/, where people look for it, but not as a machine-readable
value in the knowledge panel. Set it to true if it should be there.
host: who serves the site. Belongs in the policy, because that is
where the server logs accrue.
serverLocation: where the servers stand. With a location inside the
EU that is an argument and not an obligation — which is why it is in
the text.
logRetentionDays: how long the provider keeps access logs. It is in
their privacy statement; if in doubt leave it null, and the sentence
stays general instead of wrong.
processingAgreement: only set this to true once the data processing
agreement (Art. 28 GDPR) with netcup has actually been signed. While
false stands here, the site does not claim it.
